items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: this White Boy that we had with us, that played the job with us in Wilmington and Washington

ctx.x: So with Dizzy up there, and the brass section sitting next to him, coaxing him and trying to tell him when to play and when not to play, we made it through the night. That took care of Columbia, South Carolina. And that went on for two or three nights, heading South, even in Atlanta, Georgia. We would pick up some leftover drummer or somebody who had a set of drums or something like that, and try to make it. And finally, we got to Tampa, Florida, and we found a young kid down there, I can't remember his name…

Incidentally, I'd like to mention the fact that this White Boy that we had with us, that played the job with us in Wilmington and Washington, he was very unhappy. He was just frustrated, because he'd never been in no situation like that, and he was a New York boy, and just never had no idea that you could ever run up against a situation where he couldn't do what he wanted to, or couldn't be with who he wanted to.
